newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabian share trading up, value down.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabian share trading up, value down.

text.p: Trade picked up on the Saudi stock market in the week to Thursday, but the value of traded shares declined, figures from independent Riyadh brokers Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Sunday.
The index moved up 0.52 percent during the week to 137.25 points, the figures showed.
Volume rose to 3.23 million shares from 2.74 million shares the week before while the value of shares declined to 444.7 million riyals ($118.5 million) from 476.6 million riyals.
BFA figures showed 56 firms were traded last week. Share prices of 23 rose, 18 dropped and 15 were unchanged.
Service sector shares dominated trade, accounting for 54 percent of turnover, followed by cement shares with 21 percent.

With 513,585 shares traded, Arriyadh Development was the most active share by volume, accounting for over 15 percent of total turnover, BFA figures show. It was also the biggest gainer in the week, moving up over 10 percent to 74 riyals.
Other big gainers in the week were livestock firm Al-Mawashi Al-Mukairish 100 percent, which gained 10.3 percent to 96 riyals, and transportation company Mobarrad, up 4.5 percent at 70 riyals.
Agriculture firm SHADCO rose 4.2 percent to 25 riyals and electricity generator and distributor SCECO-Western added three riyals to 76, BFA figures show.
The biggest loser in the week was Tabouk Cement, which fell 4.6 percent to 104 riyals.
